procedure: W5 old code: the prereg names /Users/vivekgade/Documents/lattice; the orchestrator said that checkout has no workspace.py. At run time it is on next-phases at c0cdefc with lattice/workspace.py present and unmodified, so it is the primary reference (checked at run time); the detached worktree lattice-contracts-base is compared as well, both at c0cdefc.
Item notation: the prereg writes the auth item as 'as_user eve'; the code writes 'as_user:eve'. The comparison normalises ':' after as_user to a space, nothing else.
D1 item: the prereg gives no item for endpoint_missing; the expected item is the empty string (the claim 'endpoint' has none).
A CHANGED item's `relied` flag is compared only where the prereg states it (D6 false, D8 true, D9 true, C4 false); otherwise it is only recorded.
The scratch workspace manifests use absolute provider and consumer paths and sit in their own directory so one probe can hold several manifest variants over the same clones.
C2's extra blank line is placed right after the changed RUNS line (prereg: 'one extra blank line'); W1's clone gets the raise line appended and committed.
W and V probes that need a lock use the one pinned on the clean clone, as the D/C/V rule says; W1's static variant has it so that no_pin cannot mask export_failed.
A1 uses a minimal scratch project (REQUIREMENTS.md, spec.py, spec.trace.json) as the `--project` of the MCP server and Studio; the contract surfaces are workspace-level.

C3 is a slice swap at asserted line numbers (173-190 login, 191-201 me), not a str.replace; the whole-line deletes (D1, D9) assert the count of the quoted fragment, then delete the lines that hold it; L4 deletes the line including its newline.
T1 wall times are whole subprocess times (interpreter start included); the check's own elapsed_s is recorded beside them. T1 runs its own 10 static and 10 live checks.
S1's git calls use --no-optional-locks so that `git status` cannot refresh the real repository's index.
A1 reports one extra, non-counted comparison on a live link (CLI --static-only, MCP, API): the only difference allowed is the live reason.

W5 and W6 also record which lattice/workspace.py a child imports under each PYTHONPATH and that lattice.contracts is absent in the old code (a guard that the old run is old). This check was added after a first full run (35/35) and before the final run.

L5 'no request sent': a listener on 127.0.0.1:8000 (when bindable) counts connections; for hosts that cannot be observed the evidence is the exit code, the error code and the wall time (no connection attempt can complete in well under a second).
